definitions.definition: A mapping between two systems that shows they have the same structure or pattern.
definitions.example: Like how a map of a subway system and the actual subway lines have the same connections, even though the map is not the real thing.

definitions.definition: Rules or limits that a solution must follow at the edges of a problem.
definitions.example: Like saying a race car must stay on the track and not go over the wall.

definitions.definition: A set of equations that must all be true at the same time, and you solve them together.
definitions.example: Like figuring out how many apples and oranges you have if you know the total fruit and the total cost.

definitions.definition: In a general or typical case, not a special one.
definitions.example: Usually, if you have two clues, you can find two missing numbers.

definitions.definition: Only one answer that works for all the conditions.
definitions.example: Like a combination lock that opens with exactly one number sequence.

definitions.definition: To limit or restrict the possibilities.
definitions.example: Like a fence that keeps a dog in the yard.

definitions.definition: The set of all possible answers that could work.
definitions.example: All the different routes you could take to get from home to school.

definitions.definition: The claim that only one religion or belief is completely true.
definitions.example: Saying only one key opens a certain door.

definitions.definition: The most basic, final truth about what exists.
definitions.example: Like asking what everything is made of at the deepest level.

definitions.definition: Necessary features or conditions that a system must have to work.
definitions.example: A car needs wheels and an engine to be a car.

definitions.definition: Able to work or succeed.
definitions.example: A plant is viable if it can grow in the soil.

definitions.definition: When God shows truth to people.
definitions.example: Like a teacher giving you the answer to a test.

definitions.definition: To get or figure out from something else.
definitions.example: Like figuring out the recipe from tasting the cake.

definitions.definition: Latin for 'out of nothing' — creating something from nothing.
definitions.example: Like a magician pulling a rabbit from an empty hat.

definitions.definition: Beliefs that the universe flows out from God like light from a lamp, not made from nothing.
definitions.example: Like how heat comes from a fire without the fire being used up.

definitions.definition: God being beyond and above the universe, not limited by it.
definitions.example: Like an author being outside the story they wrote.

definitions.definition: God being present and active within the universe.
definitions.example: Like the author being a character inside the story.

definitions.definition: Belief that God created the universe but does not interact with it.
definitions.example: Like a clockmaker who winds the clock and leaves it alone.

definitions.definition: Belief that God is everything and everything is God.
definitions.example: Like saying the ocean is the same as every wave in it.

definitions.definition: The idea that right and wrong are real facts, not just opinions.
definitions.example: Like saying 'murder is wrong' is as true as 'water is wet'.

definitions.definition: The idea that right and wrong depend on culture or personal opinion.
definitions.example: Like saying 'murder is wrong for you but maybe not for someone else'.

definitions.definition: The ability to make choices that are not forced by anything else.
definitions.example: Like choosing chocolate or vanilla ice cream without anyone making you.

definitions.definition: The belief that every event, including your choices, is completely caused by prior events, so free will is an illusion.
definitions.example: Like a domino that has to fall because the one before it pushed it.

definitions.definition: Unearned help or favor from God.
definitions.example: Like a teacher giving you a passing grade even though you failed the test.

definitions.definition: A system that does not exchange anything (like energy or matter) with the outside.
definitions.example: Like a sealed jar with no holes.

definitions.definition: The Christian belief that God is three persons (Father, Son, Holy Spirit) in one being.
definitions.example: Like water being ice, liquid, and steam but still H2O.

definitions.definition: Belief that God is one person, not three.
definitions.example: Like saying God is just one person, like a single king.

definitions.definition: God becoming a human being, as Christians believe Jesus was God in human form.
definitions.example: Like an author writing themselves into their own story as a character.

definitions.definition: Religions that believe in only one God.
definitions.example: Christianity, Islam, and Judaism are monotheisms.

definitions.definition: The collection of all rules or limits that must be followed.
definitions.example: Like all the rules of a board game.

definitions.definition: Rules that tell you when something is not allowed or fails.
definitions.example: Like a rule that says you must be over 5 feet tall to ride a roller coaster.

definitions.definition: The need for evidence or reasoning that does not assume the conclusion.
definitions.example: Like not saying 'the Bible is true because the Bible says it is true'.

definitions.definition: The need for facts or criteria that are not influenced by personal feelings or biases.
definitions.example: Like using a ruler to measure length instead of guessing.

definitions.definition: Having more rules than needed to find a single answer, which can make the answer unique.
definitions.example: Like having three clues that all point to the same suspect.

definitions.definition: An argument that shows something is true because it meets all the required conditions.
definitions.example: Like proving a key fits a lock because it turns all the tumblers.

definitions.definition: Good reasons that make a belief reasonable to hold.
definitions.example: Like having evidence that it will rain before you take an umbrella.

definitions.definition: Believing something without good reasons or against the evidence.
definitions.example: Like believing the earth is flat despite all the photos from space.

definitions.definition: A test that checks if you can replace one thing with another and still get the same result.
definitions.example: Like trying a different key in a lock to see if it also opens.

definitions.definition: Able to be replaced by something else.
definitions.example: Like using margarine instead of butter in a recipe.

definitions.definition: Checked carefully for correctness or bias.
definitions.example: Like having a second person check your math homework.

definitions.definition: Small changes or disturbances to a system.
definitions.example: Like nudging a spinning top to see if it wobbles.

definitions.definition: Able to be proven wrong by evidence or experiment.
definitions.example: Like the claim 'all swans are white' can be proven false by finding one black swan.

definitions.definition: A weak or incorrect version of someone's argument that is easy to attack.
definitions.example: Like saying 'people who exercise are just trying to show off' instead of addressing their real reasons.

definitions.definition: Going in both directions.
definitions.example: Like a two-way street where traffic flows both ways.

definitions.definition: A matching or relationship between two things.
definitions.example: Like how a key matches a lock.

definitions.definition: Made impure or biased by something unwanted.
definitions.example: Like water with dirt in it.

definitions.definition: A statement that is true by definition, but gives no new information.
definitions.example: Like saying 'all bachelors are unmarried' — it's true but tells you nothing new.

definitions.definition: An argument that assumes what it is trying to prove.
definitions.example: Like saying 'the book is true because it was written by God, and we know it was written by God because the book says so'.

definitions.definition: The tendency to look for or interpret evidence in a way that supports what you already believe.
definitions.example: Like only reading news that agrees with your political views.

definitions.definition: The responsibility to provide evidence for a claim.
definitions.example: Like in court, the prosecutor has to prove the defendant is guilty.

definitions.definition: To save or rescue something from failure.
definitions.example: Like fixing a broken toy so it works again.

definitions.definition: People who are critical or opposed to the idea, who will look for flaws.
definitions.example: Like having a rival team check your game strategy.

definitions.definition: A major branch of Buddhism, common in Southeast Asia, that focuses on individual enlightenment.
definitions.example: Like a school that emphasizes studying hard on your own.

definitions.definition: A major branch of Buddhism, common in East Asia, that emphasizes helping all beings achieve enlightenment.
definitions.example: Like a school that encourages group projects and helping others.

definitions.definition: In Mahayana Buddhism, a person who delays their own enlightenment to help others.
definitions.example: Like a lifeguard who stays in the water to save swimmers instead of going to the beach themselves.

definitions.definition: The potential for enlightenment that exists in all beings.
definitions.example: Like an acorn having the potential to become an oak tree.

definitions.definition: A school of Mahayana Buddhism that focuses on faith in Amida Buddha to be reborn in a pure paradise.
definitions.example: Like believing that saying a special name will get you into a perfect world after death.

definitions.definition: A celestial Buddha in Pure Land Buddhism who made vows to save all who call on him.
definitions.example: Like a superhero who promises to rescue anyone who says his name.

definitions.definition: A promise made by a divine being to save others.
definitions.example: Like a lifeguard promising to save anyone who falls in the water.

definitions.definition: Having the same structure or pattern, even if the details are different.
definitions.example: Like a chessboard and a checkerboard having the same grid pattern.

definitions.definition: A school of Islamic theology that emphasizes God's absolute power and control over everything.
definitions.example: Like believing that every event, even a leaf falling, is directly caused by God.

definitions.definition: The belief that God is the only real cause of every event, and physical things are just occasions for God to act.
definitions.example: Like a puppet master directly moving every string, not just setting up a machine.

definitions.definition: A mystical branch of Islam that seeks a direct, personal experience of God.
definitions.example: Like a Christian who prays to feel close to God, not just follow rules.

definitions.definition: A direct, personal experience of being one with God or ultimate reality.
definitions.example: Like a drop of water merging with the ocean.

definitions.definition: Sufi terms: fana means 'annihilation' of the self in God; baqa means 'subsistence' or living on in God.
definitions.example: Like a candle flame being absorbed into a larger fire (fana) and then burning as part of it (baqa).

definitions.definition: A school of Hindu philosophy that teaches that only Brahman (ultimate reality) is real, and the world is an illusion.
definitions.example: Like saying the only real thing is the ocean, and waves are just temporary shapes.

definitions.definition: In Hinduism, the ultimate, unchanging reality behind everything.
definitions.example: Like the screen that a movie is projected on — the movie changes, but the screen stays the same.

definitions.definition: A school of Hindu philosophy that says Brahman is personal, and souls and matter are real parts of Brahman.
definitions.example: Like saying the ocean is one thing, but the waves and fish are real parts of it.

definitions.definition: An 11th-century Hindu philosopher who taught Vishishtadvaita.
definitions.example: Like a famous teacher who started a new school of thought.

definitions.definition: A school of Hindu philosophy that says God, souls, and matter are eternally separate and real.
definitions.example: Like saying the king, the citizens, and the castle are all real and distinct.

definitions.definition: A 13th-century Hindu philosopher who taught Dvaita.
definitions.example: Like another famous teacher with a different view from Ramanuja.

definitions.definition: Belief that God and the world are two separate realities, not the same thing.
definitions.example: Like a potter and the clay pot being different things.

definitions.definition: A difference in kind or type, not just degree.
definitions.example: Like the difference between a fruit and a vegetable, not just between an apple and an orange.

definitions.definition: Beliefs about God that someone already holds before looking at new evidence.
definitions.example: Like a scientist who already believes in God before doing an experiment.

definitions.definition: When a conclusion is hidden in the starting assumptions of an argument.
definitions.example: Like saying 'this drug works because it heals people' when you already assumed it heals people.
